questions.question_text: What is the best predictor of future sexual offences?
questions.explanation: A meta-analysis of 82 recidivism studies identified deviant sexual preferences and antisocial orientation as the major predictors of sexual recidivism for both adult and adolescent sexual offenders. Hanson RK, Morton-Bourgon KE. JOURNAL OF CONSULTING AND CLINICAL PSYCHOLOGY, 2005;73(6):1154-63.

questions.question_text: The following scale is used to assess for depression in patients with dementia
questions.explanation: The Cornell Scale for Depression in Dementia (CSDD) was specifically developed to assess signs and symptoms of major depression in patients with dementia. Because some of these patients may give unreliable reports, the CSDD uses a comprehensive interviewing approach that derives information from the patient and the informant.

questions.question_text: The following predisposes to CNS toxicity when used with Lithium
questions.explanation: Dopamine receptor antagonist antipsychotic medication, carbamazepine, clonazepam, NSAIDs, diuretics increase the risk of neurotoxicity with Lithium. Kaplan & Sadock, Synopsis of Psychiatry, 10 edn, p-1060.

questions.question_text: The following is seen in somnambulism

options.text: Complete amnesia for the transpired event
Attempt at arousal results in immediate return to full awareness

correct_answer.text: Complete amnesia for the transpired event

correct_answers.text: Complete amnesia for the transpired event

questions.explanation: The attacks in somnambulism usually last for less than 10 minutes and attempts at arousal result in gradual return to full awareness, often with marked disorientation and sleep drunkenness. There is complete amnesia for what has transpired. Lishman's Organic Psychiatry, 4th edn, pg 837.

questions.question_text: The following is a late manifestation of HIV dementia
questions.explanation: The final stages of HIV dementia are marked by severe global dementia, akinetic mutism, incontinence, paraplegia and myoclonus. Lishman's Organic Psychiatry, 4th edn, p-410.

questions.question_text: What treatment would you use for a patient with severe symptoms of pre-menstrual syndrome
questions.explanation: SSRIs have the strongest evidence for their effectiveness in the treatment of PMS. Henshaw (2007). PMS: Diagnosis, aetiology, assessment and management: REVISITING... PREMENSTRUAL SYNDROME. Advan. Psychiatr. Treat.13:139-146.

questions.question_text: The common depressive symptoms in patients with learning disability does not include
questions.explanation: Suicidal thoughts and acts occur mainly in those with mild LD and overall they are not frequently reported. Companion to Psychiatric Studies, 7 edn, p-566.

questions.question_text: A 29 year old man has been using drugs of recreation and asks you about the one which is less likely to have dependence
questions.explanation: For much of 1970s cannabis was not regarded as a drug of dependence but studies have shown features of dependence particularly in heavy users. However compared to other illicit drugs cannabis has least physical dependence. New Oxford Textbook of Psychiatry, vol 1, p-551.

questions.question_text: The hierarchy of evidence for treatment studies is

options.text: Cohort study, Case control study, case series
Expert opinion, case series, case control studies
Cohort study, expert opinion, case series

questions.explanation: Level I is evidence obtained from a single randomised controlled trial or a meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials. At least one randomised controlled trial as part of a body of literature of overall good quality and consistency addressing the specific recommendation without extrapolation. Thorax 2004;59:i13-i14.

questions.question_text: A researcher wants to evaluate the use of Magnetic resonance imaging as a screening test to identify cases of Alzheimer's dementia. They would confirm the correct diagnosis of Alzheimer's dementia by post mortem examination of the brain. Which of the following study designs would be the most appropriate for such a study?
questions.explanation: Cross sectional studies are the most appropriate study design when trying to answer questions concerning the value of screening or diagnostic tests and prevalence of a disease. Stephen Palmer and James Raftery. Economics notes: Opportunity cost. BMJ 1999;318:1551-1552.

questions.question_text: Containment is best described as

options.text: Therapist's ability to keep the emotions elicited by the patient to himself
Patient's ability to deal with anger
Patient's ability to deal with unpleasant emotions
Ability of the therapist to modify and return the patient's difficult material in a way that he(she) can tolerate
Therapist's ability to keep the actions elicited by the patient to himself

correct_answer.text: Ability of the therapist to modify and return the patient's difficult material in a way that he(she) can tolerate

correct_answers.text: Ability of the therapist to modify and return the patient's difficult material in a way that he(she) can tolerate

questions.explanation: Containment refers to a thinking function that the projected element encounters (usually the group members' projection). The therapist then uses the transference and the resulting counter-transference to understand more about the group's needs and defences. Text book of Psychotherapy in psychiatric practice, Churchill Livingstone, p-321.

questions.question_text: The percentage of women suffering domestic abuse is
questions.explanation: In a questionnaire survey of 1035 women attending east London general practices the prevalence of physical abuse in the past year from a partner or expartner was 17% and lifetime prevalence 40%. Richardson J, Coid J, Petruckevitch A, Chung WS, Moorey S, Feder G: Identifying domestic violence: cross sectional study in primary care. BMJ 2002, 324:274-278.

questions.question_text: The least common feature of Cushing's syndrome is
questions.explanation: In Cushing's syndrome 35% have depression, 16% have cognitive impairment, 9% have psychotic symptoms and 4% have euphoria. Companion to psychiatric studies, 6 edn, p-322.

questions.question_text: The most common side effect of Rivastigmine is
questions.explanation: The most common adverse effects associated with Rivastigmine are nausea, vomiting, dizziness, headache, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, anorexia, fatigue, and somnolence. Synopsis of Psychiatry, 10th edn, pg 1034.

questions.question_text: People with emotionally unstable borderline personality disorder are in
questions.explanation: Kernberg suggested that patients with BPD internalize early pathologic object relations and use primitive defense mechanisms such as splitting. This corresponds to Klein’s paranoid-schizoid position. Oxford Textbook of Psychotherapy, 2007, pg 292.

questions.question_text: The antidepressant of choice used in the treatment of moderate depression in a patient who has Myocardial infarction is
questions.explanation: When initiating antidepressant treatment in patients with recent MI or unstable angina, Sertraline is the treatment of choice and has the best evidence. NICE guidelines for depression, 2004; Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines, 2009.

questions.question_text: Which of the following psychotherapies utilises reciprocal role reversal
questions.explanation: Two forms used in Psychodrama: reciprocal role reversal (proper, classical, in situ) is used as an interpersonal conflict resolution technique. Moreno, J.L. and Moreno, Z.T. (1959) Psychodrama, vol. 2, New York: Beacon House.

questions.question_text: The sign or symptom least likely to be experienced by a person taking MDMA is
questions.explanation: Ecstasy (MDMA) is a stimulant drug, which can lead to increase in energy levels, enhanced feelings of calm, love, confidence and alertness. It can lead to anxiety, depression, paranoia & panic attacks. It is not a hallucinogen and is not known to cause hallucinations.

questions.question_text: A patient sustained fracture of facial bones from RTA is very anxious in A&E. After how long does his anxiety start to diminish to make diagnosis of acute stress reaction.
questions.explanation: An acute stress reaction defined in ICD 10 usually occurs within minutes of the triggering event and resolves rapidly,for example within few hours if the stressor is removed and within 1-3 days even if it is not

questions.question_text: An elderly gentleman has been diagnosed with delusional disorder. The following is true about delusional disorder

options.text: A persecutory subtype is the commonest one
Persecutory delusions are seen in 25% of those with diagnosis
Grandiose delusions are the most common type
The most common type is somatic delusions
Older age at onset is associated with somatic delusions

correct_answer.text: A persecutory subtype is the commonest one

correct_answers.text: A persecutory subtype is the commonest one

questions.explanation: Persecutory delusions are the most common type in all populations, (up to 60%) followed by somatic in young ages and then grandiose delusions. Yamada et al (1998) Age at onset of delusional disorder is dependent on the delusional theme. Acta Psychiatrica Scandinavica. 97(2):122-124

questions.question_text: In a positive skew graph, which of the following is true?

options.text: Mean is equal to median & mode

questions.explanation: The mean is higher than the median in positively (right) skewed distributions and lower than the median in negatively (left) skewed distributions. Companion to Psychiatric Studies, 7th edn, pg 186

questions.question_text: The most commonly used antidepressant in a patient with post-stroke depression
questions.explanation: There are more studies which show that Fluoxetine (20mg/day) is more beneficial in improving mood and motor performance. Citalopram also shows benefit but with fewer side effects. Paolucci P. Epidemiology and treatment of post-stroke depression. Neuropsychiatr Dis Treat. 2008;4(1):145-154.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the characteristic feature in transient global amnesia?

options.text: Retained ability to retain new information
Transient loss of short term memory

correct_answer.text: Transient loss of short term memory

correct_answers.text: Transient loss of short term memory

questions.explanation: Transient global amnesia manifests with a paroxysmal, transient loss of memory function. Immediate recall ability is preserved, as is remote memory; however, patients experience striking loss of memory for recent events and an impaired ability to retain new information. Lishman's Organic Psychiatry, 4th edn, pg 33

questions.question_text: According to Kernberg the psychodynamic understanding of borderline personality disorder did not include
questions.explanation: Kernberg pointed out that patients with BPD have partially intact reality testing, vulnerable to distortion because of aggression. Fully intact reality testing is not part of his model. Oxford Textbook of Psychotherapy, 2007, pg 292

questions.explanation: In descriptive statistics, a box plot or box-and-whisker diagram is a convenient way of graphically depicting groups of numerical data through their five-number summaries. Companion to Psychiatric Studies, 7th edn

questions.explanation: The box represents the interquartile range, i.e., the values between the lower and upper quartile.

questions.question_text: In the figure, the horizontal line within the box represents

questions.question_text: Please read the following precis for questions 77–81: Charman T et al. compared SCQ, SRS and CCC for screening autism. The study design used is
questions.explanation: Cross-sectional studies are appropriate when assessing the value of screening or diagnostic tests at a single point in time. Companion to Psychiatric Studies, 7th edn

questions.explanation: This study found that the CCC had a sensitivity of 0.93 (93%), the highest of the three screening tools.

questions.question_text: The screening test with the best specificity is
questions.explanation: SCQ had a specificity of 0.78 (78%), which was the highest among the three tools.

questions.question_text: Based on this data, which test would you recommend to screen for Autism spectrum disorders
questions.explanation: SCQ offers the best balance of sensitivity (0.86) and specificity (0.78) among the three tools.

questions.question_text: The gold standard test used in this study is
questions.explanation: The authors used ICD-10 research diagnostic criteria (based on ADI-R & ADOS-G findings) as the gold standard.

questions.question_text: A 65 year old lady presents with short strides, short stepping gait and progressively small cramped handwriting when tested. She also has a vertical gaze problem on examination.
questions.explanation: Progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP), also known as Steele-Richardson-Olszewski syndrome, is a neurodegenerative disease that affects cognition, eye movements, and posture. The exact cause is unknown. The cardinal manifestations of PSP are supranuclear ophthalmoplegia, pseudo bulbar palsy, prominent neck dystonia, Parkinsonism; behavioral, cognitive, and gait disturbances that cause imbalance, and frequent falls.

questions.question_text: A 15 year old boy develops non-repetitive sudden movements of his arms. He has no past history of similar problems, and the family has no degenerative illnesses. The only medical history seems to be an episode of pharyngitis nearly 6 months ago.
questions.explanation: Sydenham chorea (SD) is a neurological disorder of childhood resulting from infection via Group A beta-hemolytic streptococcus, the bacterium that causes rheumatic fever. Rapid, irregular, and aimless involuntary movements of the arms and legs, trunk, and facial muscles characterize Sydenham Chorea. It affects girls more often than boys and typically occurs between 5 and 15 years of age. Some children will have a sore throat several weeks before the symptoms begin, but the disorder can also strike up to 6 months after the fever or infection has cleared. Symptoms can appear gradually or all at once, and may include uncoordinated movements, muscular weakness, stumbling and falling, slurred speech, difficulty concentrating and writing, and emotional instability. The symptoms of SD can vary from a halting gait and slight grimacing to involuntary movements that are frequent and severe enough to be incapacitating. The random, writhing movements of chorea are caused by an auto-immune reaction to the bacterium that interferes with the normal function of a part of the brain (the basal ganglia) that controls motor movements.

questions.question_text: A 45 years old man has a history of progressive memory loss. His wife has observed him having sudden muscle movements on a number of occasions as if experiencing an electric shock momentarily.
questions.explanation: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD) is the best known of a group of diseases called prion disease, which affects a form of protein found in the central nervous system and cause dementia. Early symptoms include minor lapses of memory, mood changes and loss of interest. Within weeks, an infected person may have clumsiness and feeling muddled, become unsteady in walking, and exhibit slow or slurred speech. The symptoms progress to jerky movements, shakiness, and stiffness of limbs, incontinence and the loss of the ability to move or speak. By this stage, the person is unlikely to be aware of their surroundings or disabilities. People affected by CJD usually die within six months of onset often from pneumonia. In a minority of patients, the disease may take about two years to run its course.

questions.question_text: A 37 year old woman has repeated involuntary blinking and chin-thrusting. She is cognitively intact and has no other movement problems. She constantly uses chewing gums to conceal her facial movements.
questions.explanation: Henri Meige described in 1904 what is now commonly called oral facial dystonia. There is some variation in what has been described since in what has been called Meige's syndrome, but in all descriptions there is blinking and chin thrusting. Some patients have lip pursing or tongue movements and, for a few, the movements spread into the shoulders. The cause remains obscure, treatment less than ideal, and frustration is a major factor as it is with blepharospasm. Patients may chew gum, whistle or touch their face in an effort to lessen the movements.

questions.question_text: What was the prevalence of depression in the sample?
questions.explanation: The prevalence is the number of individuals with a disease in a population at a particular point (point prevalence) or over a period of time (period prevalence). (a+c/Grand Total; 25/74=33%).

questions.question_text: What was the sensitivity of the screening?
questions.explanation: 44% (a/a+c; 11/25). Sensitivity (True Positive): Proportion of patients testing positive out of all patients out with the disease. It is the probability that an individual with the disease will have a positive test.

questions.question_text: What was the specificity of the screening?
questions.explanation: 82% (d/b+d; 40/49). Specificity (True Negative Rate): Proportion of patients testing negative out of all patients without the disease. It is the Probability that an individual without the disease will have a negative test.

questions.question_text: What proportion of those who were screened positive was depressed?
questions.explanation: 55% (11/20). Positive LR: The odds (likelihood) of having the disease if the test result is positive.

questions.question_text: What proportion of those who were depressed screened positive?
What was the negative predictive value?
questions.explanation: 74% (d/c+d; 40/54). Negative predictive value: Measures the Proportion of patients without the disease out of all the patients testing negative. Probability that an individual with a negative test will not have the disease (Given a negative test, what is the probability of not having the disease).

questions.question_text: Attention deficit and hyperactivity disorder
questions.explanation: ADHD is more common in males at ratio of 3:1 in community samples and 9:1 in clinic samples.

questions.question_text: Autism
questions.explanation: A large review of all prevalence studies has found that the M:F ratios for Autism is around 4:1.

questions.question_text: Bulimia
questions.explanation: Bulimia is more common in females with occurrence in males that of 1/10 th in females.

questions.question_text: Aspergers syndrome
questions.explanation: With regard to gender differences, Aspergers appears to be much more common in boys. Dr. Asperger's first patients were all boys, but girls have been diagnosed with Aspergers since the 1980s. One Swedish study found the male/female ratio to be 4:1; however, the World Health Organization's ICD-10 classification gives the male to female ratio as 8 to 1.

questions.question_text: Prepubertal depression
questions.explanation: Depression in school age children is about the same in boys as in girls with some surveys indicating a slightly increased rate among boys. The rate of depression in adolescent females is double the rate in adolescent males.

LP with raised white cell count.
MRI showing focal white matter lesions.
MRI with medial temporal lobe atrophy.
SPECT scan showing hypo perfusion of occipital area.

SPECT scan showing loss of functional dopaminergic neuron terminals in the hypothalamus.

questions.question_text: A 20 year old woman is brought to you by dominating parents. She has been losing weight and her mother is concerned about this. Her father feels that she is trying to push her mother away because she refuses to put the heating on in the house, as she says she is very sensitive to it.
questions.explanation: Major clinical signs include weight loss (often accompanied by an increased appetite), anxiety, intolerance to heat, hair loss, weakness, hyperactivity, irritability, apathy, depression, polyuria, polydipsia, delirium, tremor, and sweating. Additionally, patients may present with a variety of symptoms such as palpitations and arrhythmias (notably atrial fibrillation), shortness of breath (dyspnea), loss of libido, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhoea. Long term untreated hyperthyroidism can lead to osteoporosis. In the elderly, these classical symptoms may not be present.

questions.question_text: A 16 year old girl is brought in by her parents who are concerned that she counts the calories in everything she eats and exercises excessively. Her BMI is 16.5.
questions.explanation: Anorexia nervosa is a psychiatric illness that describes an eating disorder characterized by extremely low body weight and body image distortion with an obsessive fear of gaining weight. Individuals with anorexia nervosa are known to control body weight commonly through the means of voluntary starvation, calorie counting, excessive exercise, or other weight control measures such as diet pills or diuretic drugs.

questions.question_text: A young girl is brought to you by her parents because they are concerned about her recent weight loss and also that she has fatty foul-smelling stools. You notice on examination that she has mouth ulcers and angular stomatitis.
questions.explanation: The diarrhoea characteristic of coeliac disease is pale, voluminous and malodorous. Abdominal pain and cramping, bloatedness with abdominal distension (thought to be due to fermentative production of bowel gas), angular stomatitis and mouth ulcers may be present.

questions.question_text: A 11 yr child very disruptive doesn't let you speak during assessment and also finds it difficult to sit in one place.
questions.explanation: The principal signs are inattention, impulsivity and hyperactivity at least in two different settings.

questions.question_text: A 9 yr old boy attends your clinic but doesn't touch anything in your office, likes food cooked in microwave only because that's how germs are killed and finds it difficult to complete assignments at school.
questions.explanation: The most common obsessions in children are fears of contamination, exposure to dirt, germs or disease. Typical compulsions are cleaning, checking, counting and repetitive behaviours.

questions.question_text: A 8 yr old boy brought to your clinic is reported to have tantrums in response to limits on his behaviour and also continues to engage in unacceptable behaviour as though he is trying provoke his mother.
questions.explanation: Children with ODD often argue with adults, lose their temper and are angry, resentful and easily annoyed by others.

questions.question_text: A young girl who is very aggressive and disruptive in school. She has hurt her cat by throwing it on the wall.
questions.explanation: Parental skills training is indicated here as positive parenting is known to have good outcomes.

questions.question_text: An 8 year old boy presents with auditory hallucinations, thought broadcast and delusions of reference through TV and magazines.
questions.explanation: Atypical antipsychotics, serotonin dopamine antagonists are current first line treatment for child & adolescents with schizophrenia. Childhood onset schizophrenia is a rare and severe form of schizophrenia characterized by onset of psychotic symptoms by the age of 12 yrs.

questions.question_text: A 16 year old girl presents with low mood, anhedonia, self harm behaviour and suicidal ideations.
questions.explanation: SSRIs have been suggested as the first line of treatment of antidepressant medication in adolescent depression who prefer medication. Fluoxetine has best evidence base and is licensed for use in children.

questions.question_text: Priapism
questions.explanation: Trazodone causes priapism; prolonged erection in the absence of sexual stimuli, 1 in 10,000 men.

questions.question_text: Vaginismus
questions.explanation: Vaginismus is the involuntary muscle contraction of the outer third of the vagina that interferes with penile penetration and intercourse, this condition is associated with history of sexual abuse.

questions.question_text: Premature ejaculation
questions.explanation: Premature ejaculation is when a man ejaculates before or immediately after entering the vagina. One of the common cause for this is their concern for partner satisfaction.

questions.question_text: Decreased libido
questions.explanation: All SSRIs are associated with sexual dysfunction with reduced sexual libido being the most common problem.

questions.question_text: An 18-year-old man presents to the A&E with dilated pupils, and increased appetite.
questions.explanation: Effects of cannabis intoxication include - Euphoria, relaxation,ilarity, increased appetite and glazed eyes with large pupils.

questions.question_text: A 24 year old man presents with dilated pupils, reduced appetite, auditory hallucinations, insomnia and irritability.
questions.explanation: Effects of amphetamine intoxication include - Increased alertness, pulse rate and blood pressure, and feeling of high energy. Patients with amphetamine intoxication generally present with enlarged pupils, insomnia, loss of appetite and weight, irritability, and depression.

questions.question_text: A 34 year old man presenting with slurred speech, incoordination of movements, and nystagmus.
questions.explanation: Acute alcohol and Benzodiazepine intoxication can present with similar signs including incoordination, slurring of speech, ocular signs, confusion etc.

questions.question_text: Neural tube defects in foetus.
questions.explanation: Both Valproate and Carbamazepine have been associated with spina bifida. Valproate confers a higher risk than CBZ.

questions.question_text: Atrial and Ventricular septal defects in foetus.
questions.explanation: Lithium use during pregnancy has a well known association with the cardiac malformation Ebsteins anomaly at 1:1000. The risk to foetus is maximum during 2-6 weeks after conception before many women know that they are pregnant. The risk of ASD & VSD is also increased with Lithium.

questions.question_text: Abnormally placed tricuspid valve in foetus.
questions.explanation: Lithium use during pregnancy has a well known association with the cardiac malformation Ebsteins anomaly at 1:1000. The risk to foetus is maximum during 2-6 weeks after conception before many women know that they are pregnant. The risk of ASD & VSD is also increased with Lithium.

questions.question_text: Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the new born.
questions.explanation: When taken in late pregnancy, SSRIs may increase the risk of persistent pulmonary hypertension of the new born.

questions.question_text: A 50 year old man has history of hoarding newspapers & magazines, inability to discard and feels distressed if he cant hoard.
questions.explanation: Compulsive hoarding is a form of OCD associated with excessive hoarding of possessions, inability to discard possessions, cluttering and feels distressed if they cant hoard objects and associated with other obsessions as well as compulsions.

questions.question_text: A 60 year old lady with a recent history of hoarding rubbish, change in personality and inability to learn new information.
questions.explanation: OF the options provided, this scenario is more suggestive of early onset dementia.

questions.question_text: A 15 year old boy has been collecting rare stamps and has organized these into albums for display.
questions.explanation: Collectionism is a normal phenomenon seen in children and adults with organized activity where the collected objects are kept in an order not just to hoard them.

questions.question_text: A 66 year old man living on his own in his mansion has hoarded his mansion with rubbish, refuses any help, keeps away from his family & neighbours presents with gross self neglect.
questions.explanation: Diogenes syndrome is a combination of gross self neglect, social withdrawal, hoarding and refusal of help. More common after 65 yrs and associated with psychiatric diagnosis.

questions.question_text: A old lady has been admitted to a medical ward with a 48 hour history of sudden onset distressing visual hallucinations, what is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Delirium is characterized by an acute onset, fluctuating course, attentional deficits and perceptual disturbances including hallucinations. Flaherty JH et al. J Am Med Dir Assoc 2007;8(5):2735.

questions.question_text: The scale used to screen for cognitive impairment in people with Downs syndrome is
questions.explanation: The Dementia Questionnaire for Persons with Mental Retardation (DMR) is one of the instruments used for dementia screening in intellectual disability. Deb et al. Br J Psychiatry 2007;190:440-444.

questions.question_text: The following is not seen in Lennox Gastaut syndrome

options.text: Diffuse slow spike and wave discharges against the background with paroxysms of fast activity
There is a strong genetic component in the aetiology
Onset between 1 and 8 years of age

correct_answer.text: There is a strong genetic component in the aetiology

correct_answers.text: There is a strong genetic component in the aetiology

questions.explanation: A strong genetic component is characteristic of other epilepsies (e.g., myoclonic seizures), not classic Lennox–Gastaut syndrome. Lishman's Organic Psychiatry, 4th edn, p-318.

questions.question_text: A 68-year old man with a previous diagnosis of depression has been recently diagnosed with Parkinson's disease. His wife complains that in the last 2 weeks he has been sending her sexually-explicit messages, and accusing her of having an affair. What is the most likely drug to have caused this?
questions.explanation: Ropinirole (a D3-preferring dopamine agonist) can cause compulsive behaviours such as hypersexuality and gambling. Bostwick JM et al. Mayo Clin Proc. 2009;84(4):310-316.

questions.question_text: What is the lifetime risk of suicide in alcohol dependence?
questions.explanation: The lifetime risk of suicide among individuals with alcohol dependence treated in out-patient settings is about 2.2%. Sher L. QJM 2006;99(1):57-61.

questions.question_text: A 39 year old lady has had many recurrent depressive episodes in the past and one episode of hypomania. The best medication to prevent relapse for her is:
questions.explanation: Lamotrigine has demonstrated efficacy in preventing depressive relapse, especially in Bipolar II disorder with predominant depressive polarity. NICE Bipolar disorder guideline 2006.

questions.question_text: A 38-year old lady with multiple sclerosis, presents to her GP with depression. Her GP is concerned, and asks you what medication may have caused her depression?
questions.explanation: Corticosteroid therapy can precipitate mood changes including depression. Meta-analyses show no clear increase in depression with interferon-beta. Nikfar S. et al. Clin Ther. 2010;32(11):1871-1888.

questions.question_text: A drug A is compared with placebo in the treatment of a condition and the outcome used is the time to hospital admission. Which is the best statistic to use to compare the two interventions?
questions.explanation: The log-rank test is the standard nonparametric test to compare survival distributions (time-to-event data) between two groups.

questions.question_text: The most common side effect of Rivastigmine is
questions.explanation: The most common adverse effects with Rivastigmine include nausea, vomiting, dizziness, headache, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, anorexia, fatigue, and somnolence. Synopsis of Psychiatry, 10th edn, pg 1034.

questions.question_text: You are asked to write a court report for a man convicted of a sexual assault, which of the following is most likely to increase his risk of subsequent offending?
questions.explanation: An antisocial orientation (e.g., history of non-sexual violent offences) and deviant sexual preferences are the major predictors of sexual recidivism. Hanson RK, Morton-Bourgon KE. J Consult Clin Psychol. 2005;73(6):1154-1163.

questions.question_text: Publication bias can be detected by using a
questions.explanation: A funnel plot (effect size vs. study precision) is used to detect asymmetry suggesting publication bias. Light RJ & Pillemer DB. Summing up: The Science of Reviewing Research. 1984.

questions.question_text: The following are correct about school refusal except

options.text: Parents are aware of the absence
Child does not comply with completing homework
Severe emotional distress about attending school
Child often persuades parents to be allowed to stay at home

correct_answer.text: Child does not comply with completing homework

correct_answers.text: Child does not comply with completing homework

questions.explanation: Children with school refusal do comply with homework at home and are willing to complete work outside school. Fremont WP. AFP. 2003;68(7):1407-1412.

questions.question_text: A couple have one child with Down's syndrome. Which of the following chromosomal findings in the child would increase the chance of their second child having Down's?
questions.explanation: Familial translocation involving chromosome 21 increases recurrence risk to about 1 in 10. Nontranslocation trisomy 21 carries ~1% recurrence risk. Shorter Oxford Textbook of Psychiatry, 5th edn, p 718.

questions.question_text: The treatment of choice in childhood PTSD is
questions.explanation: Trauma-focused CBT has the strongest RCT evidence for efficacy in childhood PTSD. NICE PTSD guideline 2005.

questions.question_text: The most common genetic change leading to Down's syndrome is
questions.explanation: About 95% of Down's syndrome cases are due to nondisjunction trisomy 21. Shorter Oxford Textbook of Psychiatry, 5th edn.

questions.question_text: What treatment would you use for a patient with severe symptoms of pre-menstrual syndrome
questions.explanation: SSRIs (e.g., Fluoxetine) have the strongest evidence for effectiveness in PMS. Henshaw (2007). Adv Psychiatr Treat. 2007;13:139-146.

questions.question_text: Which is the treatment of choice in childhood obsessive compulsive disorder?
questions.explanation: Clinical consensus recommends psychological treatment (CBT with exposure/response prevention) as first-line in pediatric OCD. NICE OCD guideline 2006.

questions.question_text: The following is true regarding pharmacokinetics in the elderly:

options.text: There is 25% reduction in GFR in 80-year olds
The distribution of lipid soluble drugs is increased
No change in hepatic function with age
The rate of absorption is slower
The absorption is less than in younger adults

correct_answer.text: The rate of absorption is slower

correct_answers.text: The rate of absorption is slower

questions.explanation: Elderly have increased body fat, reduced total body water and lower albumin, leading to increased volume of distribution and longer half-life for lipophilic drugs.

questions.question_text: What is the risk of recurrence of postpartum psychosis in subsequent pregnancies?
questions.explanation: Puerperal recurrences occur in about 20–25% of subsequent pregnancies. New Oxford Textbook of Psychiatry, vol 2, 2000, p 1203.

questions.question_text: Which is the most suitable alpha 2 agonist for a patient with opioid dependence with tendency to have low blood pressure?
questions.explanation: Lofexidine causes less hypotension than clonidine and may be preferred in patients who do not wish to use opioids. Walsh et al. Addiction. 2003;98(4):427-439.

questions.question_text: Which of the following may worsen psoriasis?
questions.explanation: Lithium can aggravate or precipitate psoriasis. Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines, 10th edn, p 129.

questions.question_text: A woman with breast cancer has developed moderate depression. She is on tamoxifen treatment. Which antidepressant would you avoid in this lady?
questions.explanation: Fluoxetine (and paroxetine) are potent CYP2D6 inhibitors that reduce active tamoxifen metabolite levels. Jin et al. J Natl Cancer Inst. 2005;97(1):30-39.

questions.question_text: The diagnosis with most heritability among the following is?
questions.explanation: ADHD has heritability estimates >70%, among the highest of common psychiatric disorders. Rutter & Taylor, Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, p 190.

questions.question_text: Smoking in a pregnant lady can lead to the following in the child

options.text: A syndrome similar to fetal alcohol syndrome

questions.explanation: Smoking in pregnancy is associated with miscarriage, intrauterine growth restriction and premature delivery. Companion to Psychiatric Studies, 8th edn, p-788.

questions.question_text: A young man comes to your outpatient clinic concerned that he may develop problem drinking. His father and his aunt were heavy drinkers and were dependent on alcohol. What is his increase in risk of becoming alcohol dependent?
questions.explanation: First-degree relatives of alcohol-dependent probands have about a twofold increased risk. Nurnberger JE Jr et al. Arch Gen Psychiatry. 2004;61(12):1246-1256.

questions.question_text: Which drug has the best evidence to treat acute mania?
questions.explanation: Lithium has the longest and strongest evidence base for efficacy in acute mania. NICE Bipolar disorder guideline 2006.

questions.question_text: Subcultural causes for mild learning disability does not include
questions.explanation: Higher rates of mild learning disability are seen in lower social classes, poverty, overcrowding and large families; not high social class. Companion to Psychiatric Studies, 8th edn, p-545.

questions.question_text: You are seeing the parents of a 26 year old gentleman under your care. He has schizophrenia and they want to know his prognosis. What type of schizophrenia has the best prognosis?
questions.explanation: Paranoid schizophrenia carries the best prognosis, with later onset, good premorbid adjustment and fewer negative symptoms. Companion to Psychiatric Studies, 8th edn, p-399.

questions.question_text: Which of the following medications could cause a decrease in plasma lithium level?
questions.explanation: Theophylline increases renal clearance of lithium and can lower plasma lithium levels. Kaplan & Sadock, Synopsis of Psychiatry, 10th edn, p-560.

questions.question_text: Neuroimaging studies in patients with OCD show
questions.explanation: PET studies show increased metabolism in orbitofrontal cortex and caudate nuclei in OCD, which improves with treatment. Companion to Psychiatric Studies, 8th edn, p-89.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is most commonly seen in Progressive Supranuclear Palsy?
questions.explanation: Bradyphrenia (slowed thought processes) is common in PSP. Other features include vertical gaze palsy, backward falls and neurofibrillary tangles in subcortical structures. Lishman's Organic Psychiatry, 4th edn, p-776.

questions.question_text: A 70-year old woman whose sister was diagnosed with Alzheimer's wants to know her risk relative to the general population.
questions.explanation: First-degree relatives have a 3–4 fold increased risk of Alzheimer's disease, though actual lifetime incidence is lower. Liddell & Lovestone. Br J Psychiatry 2001;178:7-11.

questions.question_text: In Prader-Willi syndrome the following is commonly seen
questions.explanation: Hyperphagia and compulsive overeating are hallmark features of Prader–Willi syndrome. Synopsis of Psychiatry, 10th edn, p-1148.

questions.question_text: A pregnant woman dependent on heroin wishes detoxification. Which of the following is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Methadone maintenance is preferred in pregnancy to reduce maternal/fetal risk. Detoxification may be attempted with caution but methadone remains first-line. Lingford-Hughes et al. J Psychopharmacol. 2004;18(3):293-335.

questions.question_text: What is the term used to describe the loss of productivity to patients and employers when patients had to seek treatment?
questions.explanation: Indirect costs capture lost work days and productivity. Direct costs are for treatment itself; intangible costs cover pain and suffering. Greenhalgh T. How to Read a Paper, 2nd edn, p-154.

questions.question_text: The cost of forgoing an established treatment whilst opting for a new treatment is termed as
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the benefit foregone by not using resources in the next best alternative. Palmer S & Raftery J. BMJ 1999;318:1551-1552.

questions.question_text: A depressed patient is on Venlafaxine 225 mg and Mirtazapine 45 mg but is not improving, which of the following do you do?

options.text: Stop Venlafaxine and augment with lithium
Stop both and start another antidepressant
Stop Mirtazapine and augment with lithium

questions.explanation: When combination SSRI/SNRI plus mirtazapine fails (STAR*D stage 4), ECT should be considered for treatment-resistant depression, especially if rapid response is needed. NICE Depression guideline 2009.

questions.question_text: A 29 year old man has been using drugs of recreation and asks you about the one which is less likely to have dependence?

A 36 year old man with moderate depression has been given a trial of fluoxetine, and has shown a partial response, with symptoms of decreased sleep still persisting. Which of the following medication would be a useful strategy for augmentation?
questions.explanation: The current NICE guidance (Oct 2009) advises using Lithium, Mirtazapine, Mianserin, Antipsychotics for augmenting antidepressants in treatment of depression in adults. In this case of a person with sleep problems, it may be useful to use Mirtazapine as an augmenting agent. Depression in Adults. NICE 2009.

questions.question_text: A pregnant woman who had a previous depressive episode is now euthymic and not on any psychotropic medications. What is her risk of depressive relapse in the postnatal period?
questions.explanation: Previous history of depression is one of the strongest predictors of Postnatal depression, with studies the chance of a woman with previous history of depression developing postnatal depression being 1:3. Bloch M et al., Risk Factors for early postpartum depressive symptoms. General Hospital Psychiatry 2006:28(1):3-8.

questions.question_text: The following is true regarding learning disability and PTSD

options.text: People with Learning disability not affected by traumatic events
Accidents are the commonly experienced traumatic event
People with learning disability overdiagnosed with PTSD
Sexual assault is the commonly experienced precipitating trauma
OCD is the common presentation after traumatic events

correct_answer.text: Sexual assault is the commonly experienced precipitating trauma

correct_answers.text: Sexual assault is the commonly experienced precipitating trauma

questions.explanation: People with learning disability develop PTSD at a rate comparable to the able population when exposed to trauma. Each person had suffered at least two types of trauma. The most frequently experienced was sexual abuse by multiple perpetrators (commonly starting in childhood), physical abuse or life-threatening neglect committed with some other active abuse or trauma. Post-traumatic stress disorder in people with learning disability, Jane McCarthy, Advances in Psychiatric Treatment (2001) 7:163-169.

questions.question_text: A patient who has recently completed an inpatient detoxification from opiates would like to be prescribed something that will help to prevent relapse. Which of the following has the best evidence base for maintenance treatment for this person?
questions.explanation: Buprenorphine and Methadone have been recommended as 1st line in the maintenance treatment of opiate dependence. Naltrexone is used in abstinence-based treatments to prevent relapse, not as first-line. Due to shorter half-life and parenteral route Naloxone is not a practical option. NICE guidelines, 2007.

questions.question_text: The pattern of inheritance of Klinefelter’s syndrome
questions.explanation: Klinefelter syndrome is not inherited; it usually occurs as a random event during the formation of reproductive cells (eggs and sperm). An error in cell division called nondisjunction results in a reproductive cell with an abnormal number of chromosomes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following would be the most appropriate next step for someone who has been unsuccessfully treated with both buprenorphine and methadone?
questions.explanation: Injectable diacetylmorphine (heroin) was more effective than oral methadone, but because of risks of overdose and seizures, prompt medical intervention should be available. Methadone remains the treatment of choice for most, but injectable heroin can be an option if adequate doses of methadone and buprenorphine do not give desired results. Brissette S, Marsh DC, et al. N Engl J Med, 2009;361:777-786.

questions.question_text: The following is true with regards to Autism.

options.text: Not associated with Fragile X syndrome
Rates have been found to be higher in patients exposed to the MMR vaccine
Perinatal complications not associated with autism

questions.explanation: Early studies of twins estimated the heritability of autism to be more than 90%. Monozygotic concordance is >90%. Autism is seen in around 25% of male patients with fragile X and 6% of females. Perinatal complications are associated with autism (higher prevalence, though not necessarily causal). Rutter (2000); Abrahams & Geschwind (2008).

questions.question_text: According to NINCDS-ARDA criteria, a diagnosis of Alzheimer’s dementia is unlikely if

options.text: Progressive deterioration of specific cognitive function
Plateaux in the course of progression
There is gait disturbance at the onset of illness
Onset is only after forty years of age

correct_answer.text: There is gait disturbance at the onset of illness

correct_answers.text: There is gait disturbance at the onset of illness

questions.explanation: Diagnosis of AD is unlikely if there are focal neurological signs and incoordination early in the course, seizures or gait disturbances at the onset or very early in the illness. Companion to Psychiatric Studies, 8th Edn, p658.

questions.question_text: A depressed woman is prescribed a tricyclic antidepressant. Which of the following is she more likely to tolerate?
questions.explanation: Lofepramine has lower incidence of side effects and is less dangerous in overdose; newer TCAs (lofepramine, dothiepin) show greater tolerability than older TCAs. Department of Health, Prescribing figures, 2002.

questions.question_text: The mechanism of action of Modafinil includes
questions.explanation: Modafinil is reported to act by alpha-1 agonism accounting for its alertness, and activates hypocretin-producing neurons. Kaplan & Saddock, 10th edn, p1099.

questions.question_text: Which instrument is used for assessing psychopathy?
questions.explanation: The most widely used measure of psychopathy is the Hare Psychopathy Checklist Revised (PCL-R). It is a 20-item rating scale scored from semi-structured interview and collateral information and has been validated in forensic samples.

questions.question_text: Autism is most likely to be associated with which of the following:
questions.explanation: Hyperactivity is common in autism. (Goodman & Scott, Child Psychiatry, 2002, p 43.)

questions.question_text: The following is a feature of advanced heroin withdrawal in a young man you see in A&E
questions.explanation: Late symptoms of opioid withdrawal include abdominal cramping, diarrhoea, dilated pupils, goose bumps, nausea and vomiting. (Revision Notes in Psychiatry – Puri & Hall, 2nd Ed., 2004, p 353.)

questions.question_text: A patient has been recently diagnosed with Vascular dementia. A past history of cerebrovascular disease in this patient would be most evident by which of the following?
questions.explanation: History of cerebrovascular disease is suggested by slurred speech, incontinence, ataxia, falls, weakness, etc. (Lishman’s Organic Psychiatry, 4th Ed., p 568.)

questions.question_text: The ideal value for kappa is
questions.explanation: Kappa measures inter-rater reliability. If raters are in complete agreement then κ = 1; no agreement beyond chance gives κ = 0. (Companion to Psychiatric Studies, 8th Ed., p 159.)

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a significant variable predictor of sexual offence recidivism in offenders with intellectual disabilities?
questions.explanation: Significant predictors were allowances made by staff, antisocial attitude, poor relationship with mother, denial of crime, sexual abuse in childhood, erratic attendance, and poor response to treatment. (Lindsay et al., J Appl Res Intell Disabil, 2004;17(4):299-305.)

questions.question_text: The following is true about cocaine users

options.text: Mood disorders usually precedes the onset of cocaine related disorders
Alcoholism is the commonest lifetime comorbidity
Schizophrenia is one of the commonest comorbidties
Cocaine use is on the rise
Anxiety disorders commonly precede the onset of cocaine related disorders

correct_answer.text: Alcoholism is the commonest lifetime comorbidity

correct_answers.text: Alcoholism is the commonest lifetime comorbidity

questions.explanation: Current cocaine use is on the decline, with anxiety disorders, ADHD and antisocial PD commonly preceding the development of cocaine‐related disorders.

questions.question_text: Which psychotherapy utilises reciprocal role reversal?
questions.explanation: In Psychodrama, reciprocal (classical) role reversal is used to deal with social perceptions and interpersonal conflict resolution. (Moreno & Moreno, Psychodrama vol 2, 1959.)

questions.question_text: In a survey done by a community team on patients in the community the response rates were very low. The response rates can be improved by

options.text: By doing home visits and interviewing patients
Sending the questionnaire to a large population sample
Using all the questionnaires in English

questions.explanation: Studies show response rates improve with incentives, often raising rates from 15% to 50%, though one must check for incentive‐related bias. (Shelton, Measuring and Improving Patient Satisfaction, p 169.)

questions.question_text: The pattern of inheritance of Pick’s disease.
questions.explanation: Approximately 10–27% of Pick's (frontotemporal dementia) patients show autosomal dominant inheritance. (Seelaar et al., J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry 2010.)

questions.question_text: Which of the following represent ‘acting out’ during therapy in an individual with antisocial personality disorder?

options.text: Praising the therapist in the session when actually angry with the therapist
Leaving the session suddenly and getting drunk

correct_answer.text: Leaving the session suddenly and getting drunk

correct_answers.text: Leaving the session suddenly and getting drunk

questions.explanation: Acting out is enacting an unconscious wish or fantasy impulsively as a way of avoiding painful affect. It may involve gross misuse of drugs or alcohol and sudden departures from the therapeutic setting. (Oxford Textbook of Psychotherapy, 2005, pp. 5, 269–270.)

questions.question_text: The database that provides systematic coverage of the psychological literature from the 1800s to the present is
questions.explanation: PsycINFO is an abstract database providing systematic coverage of the psychological literature from the 1800s to the present. (BMJ 1997;314:572.)

questions.question_text: The most common symptom of delirium is
questions.explanation: In 100 delirium cases, sleep–wake cycle disturbances occurred in 97%, making it the most frequent symptom. (Meagher DJ et al. Br J Psychiatry 2007;190:135–141.)

questions.question_text: What is the mode of inheritance of Pick’s disease?
questions.explanation: An autosomal dominant mode of inheritance is found in 10–27% of Pick’s dementia patients. (Seelaar H et al. J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry 2010.)

questions.question_text: What proportion of sexual offenders have no prior history of criminal offence?
questions.explanation: Home Office data show that approximately 79% of those imprisoned for offences against children and 75% against adults had no previous sexual convictions. (Home Office report.)

questions.question_text: A 29 year-old man who is on Quetiapine 600 mg has QTc 500 ms + T-wave morphology on routine ECG. What would be the next step of management?

options.text: Reduce dose of quetiapine and repeat ECG with an option of referring to cardiology
No intervention so long as the patient is asymptomatic
Cross-taper in order to start risperidone and repeat ECG in 2 weeks
Stop quetiapine and then add risperidone

correct_answer.text: Stop quetiapine and then add risperidone

correct_answers.text: Stop quetiapine and then add risperidone

questions.explanation: QTc > 500 ms carries a definite risk of arrhythmia. The causative drug should be stopped and switched to one with lower QT-prolonging liability (e.g., aripiprazole). (Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines, 10th Ed.)

questions.question_text: A young woman comes to see you one month after the death of her sister. She describes low mood, poor sleep and that she is hearing her sister’s voice. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Stage II of the grief reaction (weeks to ~6 months) can include sadness, poor sleep, diminished appetite, illusions, hallucinations (e.g., hearing the deceased’s voice) and social withdrawal. (Shorter Oxford Textbook of Psychiatry, 5th Edn.)

questions.question_text: Which one of the following would be the most commonly seen symptom in velocardiofacial syndrome?
questions.explanation: Learning disability is usually mild to moderate in velocardiofacial syndrome; some have specific learning disorders without global intellectual impairment. (Companion to Psychiatric Studies, 8th Edn.)

questions.question_text: A man has stopped drinking alcohol for about three months having previously been dependent. Which medication will be best to help keep him abstinent?
questions.explanation: Acamprosate and naltrexone improve abstinence rates; acamprosate is preferred as it does not require supervised intake. (BAP Guidelines 2004.)

questions.question_text: A 20 year-old man presents to A&E with Phencyclidine intoxication. The signs/symptoms that he can present with include
questions.explanation: PCP intoxication features include nystagmus, hypertension, tachycardia, diminished responsiveness to pain, ataxia, dysarthria, muscle rigidity, seizures or coma. (DSM-IV TR.)

questions.question_text: A middle aged man is suffering from depression and has been prescribed fluoxetine by GP, which has made some improvement in his mood, but is having problems with sleep. Which antidepressant would you prescribe?
questions.explanation: Mirtazapine is the drug of choice in this case because of its sedative action and is an effective alternative to SSRIs as second-line treatment in depression. (NICE guidance for depression, 2009.)

questions.question_text: The most appropriate measure to explain about treatment response of a medication to a patient would be
questions.explanation: The number needed to treat (NNT) is the number of patients who need to be treated for one to benefit compared with a control. It is a useful measure of treatment response. (Altman & Bland, BMJ.)

questions.question_text: The rate of relapse of mood disorder in the postnatal period in a woman with a preexisting diagnosis of bipolar disorder is
questions.explanation: Recent studies estimate that over 25–50% of women with bipolar disorder will experience relapse in the first 6 months postnatally if not taking mood stabilisers. (Companion to Psychiatric Studies, 8th Edn, p 790.)

questions.question_text: Regarding aggression in ADHD, which of the following is not correct?

options.text: Aggression is due to adverse intrafamily relationships
75% of children with ADHD have aggression
Aggression is not a core feature of ADHD
Aggression can be a response to reactions from school staff & peers

questions.explanation: While adverse family dynamics can exacerbate behavioural problems, aggression in ADHD is primarily related to underlying neurobiological factors rather than being directly caused by intrafamily relationships alone. (Kaplan & Saddock, Synopsis of Psychiatry, 10th ed., p 1208.)

questions.question_text: The kappa is used to measure
questions.explanation: Cohen’s kappa coefficient is a statistical measure of inter-rater agreement for categorical items, accounting for chance agreement. (Companion to Psychiatric Studies, 8th Edn, p 159.)

questions.question_text: The last stage according to Prochaska and DiClemente’s model of change of behavior is
questions.explanation: In the maintenance stage, the new behaviours (e.g., abstinence) are sustained long term. (Zernig et al., Handbook of Alcoholism, 2000.)

questions.question_text: A 15 year old boy presents with a moderate depressive illness. He is otherwise fit and intelligent and does not have suicidal ideas or plans. The treatment of choice for this boy would be
questions.explanation: For moderate to severe depression in young people, NICE recommends a specific psychological therapy (individual CBT, interpersonal therapy or family therapy) as first-line treatment. (NICE 2006 guidance.)
